mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly defines a chemical compound?

options.A: A substance made of two or more elements chemically combined in a fixed proportion.
options.B: A pure substance consisting of only one type of atom.
options.C: A mixture of two or more substances that can be separated by physical means.
options.D: A substance that can be broken down into simpler substances by physical methods.

mcqs.answer: A substance made of two or more elements chemically combined in a fixed proportion.
mcqs.explanation: A compound is formed when two or more different elements combine chemically in a definite, fixed ratio (e.g., H₂O). Option B describes an element, C describes a mixture, and D describes a physical separation, not a chemical compound.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes an element from a compound?

options.A: Elements consist of only one type of atom; compounds consist of two or more different atoms chemically bonded.
options.B: Elements can be broken into simpler substances by chemical reactions; compounds cannot be broken down.
options.C: Elements have a fixed composition; compounds have a variable composition.
options.D: Elements are always gases, whereas compounds are always solids.

mcqs.answer: Elements consist of only one type of atom; compounds consist of two or more different atoms chemically bonded.
mcqs.explanation: Elements are pure substances made of identical atoms. Compounds are formed when different elements combine chemically in fixed ratios. Options B, C, and D are incorrect misconceptions about elements and compounds.

mcqs.learning_point: Recognise that compounds have fixed composition
mcqs.question: Which statement correctly reflects the fixed composition of a chemical compound?

options.A: Water (H₂O) always contains hydrogen and oxygen in a mass ratio of 2:16, regardless of its source.
options.B: Air always contains nitrogen and oxygen in a fixed mass ratio of 78:21.
options.C: Table salt (NaCl) can have varying ratios of Na to Cl in different samples.
options.D: A sugar solution can have varying proportions of sugar and water.

mcqs.answer: Water (H₂O) always contains hydrogen and oxygen in a mass ratio of 2:16, regardless of its source.
mcqs.explanation: Compounds like water have a definite composition; every molecule of H₂O has exactly two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom, giving a constant mass ratio. Air, table salt, and sugar solutions are mixtures where component proportions can vary.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly differentiates a compound from a mixture?

options.A: In a compound, the constituent elements are chemically combined in a fixed ratio; in a mixture, the components retain their individual chemical identities and can be present in any proportion.
options.B: A compound can be separated into its elements by simple filtration; a mixture cannot be separated by any method.
options.C: Compounds always consist of metals; mixtures always consist of non‑metals.
options.D: The boiling point of a compound is always higher than that of any mixture containing the same substances.

mcqs.answer: In a compound, the constituent elements are chemically combined in a fixed ratio; in a mixture, the components retain their individual chemical identities and can be present in any proportion.
mcqs.explanation: Compounds involve chemical bonding with a definite composition, while mixtures are physical combinations where each component keeps its own properties and can vary in proportion. Options B, C, and D are incorrect statements about separation methods, composition, and boiling points.
